ui.w_forums: You're in the Forum! Can I help with a question about it?
ui.w_shop: You're in the Shop! Any question about coins or payments?
ui.w_profile: You're on your profile! Can I explain anything here?
ui.w_list: You're on your list! Need help organizing it?
ui.w_animes: Looking for something to watch? I can help with filters and search.
ui.w_default: What would you like to talk about? Pick an area, or type your question!
ui.m_menu: Sure! Pick an area (or type your question and I'll try to understand 😉):
ui.m_sources: Sources and episodes, good choice! What's going on?
ui.m_player: Player and subtitles! Tell me what you need:
ui.m_account: Account and profiles! What would you like to know?
ui.m_community: Community! This is where the conversation happens 🗣️
ui.m_shop: XP, coins and shop — the fun part! 🎮
ui.m_app: The app and the team! What would you like to know?
ui.fallback: Hmm, that one has me thinking… 🤔 I don't know how to answer that yet. Pick an area below, rephrase the question, or talk to the team, who can sort it out.

ui.bye: See you soon! Enjoy your episodes! 🍿
ui.how_are: I'm great, warming up the virtual popcorn! 🍿 And you? How can I help?
ui.still_here: I'm here, yes! 👋 Tell me what you need.

ui.who_q: I'm the AnimeLayer assistant! I don't have an official name yet… give the team some ideas 😄 I can help with sources, subtitles, account, community and much more.

ui.bored: Out of ideas? On Home you'll find Trending and the Current Season, and “Continue watching” keeps your spot. If you tell me the genre you like, I'll try to help with the filters 😉

ui.insult2: I understand you're upset, really. 🙏 If you want to vent about a real problem with the app, tell me what it is, or talk to the team, who can look at your case.

ui.handoff_again: I get it! This really needs a person from the team. Describe what happened and what you've already tried: they'll answer you there.
ui.sensitive: I'm sorry you're going through this. 💛 I'm not the right help for it, but talking to someone you trust or to the emergency services in your area can really help. You are not alone.
ui.injection: Haha, nice try! 😄 I'm just an assistant with answers written by the team: there's nothing to unlock. How can I help with AnimeLayer?
ui.off_third: I don't know much about other apps and I'd rather not compare 🙂 Each has its own style. About AnimeLayer, though: ask away!
ui.nonsense: Hmm, that didn't sound like a question 😅 If it was by accident, no worries! Tell me what you need, or pick a topic.
ui.off1: Hmm, that's a bit outside my world 😅 I can only talk about AnimeLayer: sources, subtitles, account, community, XP… How can I help you with those?
ui.off2: I still don't know that one 🙈 I really am only the AnimeLayer assistant. If it's about the app, pick an area; otherwise, it's better to ask someone who knows.
ui.off3: I don't think I can help you with this. 🙂 If you need something about AnimeLayer, pick a topic or talk to the team; I'll stay here.
ui.broad: I don't have an exact answer for that, but I found these topics that mention it. Does one of them help? 🤔
ui.tie: Hmm, I'm not sure what you mean, but it might be one of these. Which one? 🤔
ui.no_profile: To talk to the team you need an active profile. Pick a profile and try again.

facts: Did you know AnimeLayer is available in 12 languages? 🌍
Did you know an episode is marked as watched automatically after 5 minutes of real playback? ⏱️
Did you know that while you watch an episode, the next one is already downloading in the background? 🚀
Did you know you can see your position in every ranking on your profile? 🏆
Did you know you can change the color, size and outline of the subtitles? 🎨
Did you know that at the end of each month, the podium of each ranking wins trophies? 🥇

l: Let's find out what's going on. First: do you already have an addon active in Settings?

fontes_com_addon.t: I have an addon but there are no sources
l: Then the problem is usually one of these: the episode hasn't come out yet, the addon doesn't have that title, or the addon is slow or down (I wait a few seconds for each one). Try opening another episode of the same title: if that one has sources, the problem is only with that episode.

Another thing to try: having more than one addon active increases your chances, because each one has different things. You can also go back and open the sources again. If it's a freshly released episode, it can take a few hours.

An addon is like an extension that brings episode sources to the app. AnimeLayer doesn't come with any installed and doesn't recommend any: you're the one who chooses. We organize, keep track and bring the community together.

k: how do i add an addon
how do i know if the addon is active
l: In Settings, on the Addons tab, you paste the address of the addon you want to use into the field and press “Install addon”. AnimeLayer doesn't suggest any, so the address comes from you.

If you pasted the address and it doesn't work: the app adds /manifest.json at the end by itself if it's missing, but the address may be wrong or the addon may be down. Also check that the addon's switch is on.
Freshly aired episodes take a while to get sources: sometimes a few hours. Subscribe to the title and I'll notify you when a new episode comes out.

Some sources take longer, especially the less popular ones. If it goes past a minute or two, go back and pick another source: that usually fixes it. While you wait, enjoy my jokes on the loading screen 😉
You can use the source filters (quality, size, language) to pick a lighter one. Sources with lots of people sharing start faster.

In the source list you see each one's quality, size and language. The lighter ones start faster; the heavier ones look better. At the top there are filters by quality, language and size. When you go to the next episode, I try to keep the same source you chose.

In the player, the audio button lets you pick the track when the file has more than one (for example, the original and a dub). It depends on the source: the source list has a filter by audio language, so you can look for the ones with what you want.
Check the volume in the player and on your system. If there's still no sound, try another source: sometimes the audio track is missing.
If it always happens, on several sources, tell the team which system you're on (Windows, Android…).
A black screen with sound is usually a problem with that source. Try another one.
If it happens on all of them, tell the team which system you're on and which title, so they can take a look.
In the player, the subtitles button lets you pick the language. Subtitles depend on what the source brings: if one doesn't have your language, another may.
If there's no subtitle in your language, the app also looks for external subtitles and has an automatic translation (beta) that translates an existing subtitle keeping the timing.
In the player's subtitle options you can delay or advance the text until it's right. If one source is always off, try another.
In the player's subtitle settings you change the font, color, size, outline, shadow and position on the screen. Everything is saved for next time.
When the opening or ending starts, a skip button appears (the timings come from a community database). Not all episodes have those timings, so it doesn't always show up.
The player has live color correction: brightness, contrast, saturation and gamma, without leaving the episode.

Picture-in-Picture mode puts the video in a small window on top of everything else so you can keep watching while you do something else. On Android it's native; on the computer it's a floating window.

On your phone, swipe on the right side of the screen for volume and on the left for brightness. There are also buttons to skip forward and back 10 seconds, and the progress bar shows how much is already loaded: tap it to jump to any point.
While you watch an episode, the next one is already downloading in the background, so it usually starts almost right away. When you move on, I try to keep the same source you chose.

k: how do i mark as watched
l: The episode is marked as watched automatically after 5 minutes of real playback (if you pause, the time stops). You can also mark or unmark it by hand in the episode list.
If it didn't mark, check that you have an active profile and that you're online. If it keeps happening, let the team know.

k: pick up where i left off
l: On Home you have the “Continue watching” shelf with the last episodes you were watching, so you can resume with one click.
The player has real-time statistics (speed, connections and percentage downloaded) for those who like numbers.

On the computer, episodes are stored temporarily and the app cleans them up by itself. To choose where they go, open Settings, General tab, “Downloads folder”: you pick the folder and restart the app.
The player has a fullscreen button, next to the controls.
Signing in is done with Discord or Google, without a password: you press the button and authorize. There is no email and password sign-up, on purpose, for security.
If you can't sign in, check that you're online and using the same account as always. If it keeps happening, tell the team what shows on the screen.
You can have several profiles on the same account, each with its own list, progress and XP, like on Netflix. You create and pick them on the profiles screen when you sign in.

On your profile press “Edit profile”: there you change the name (it has a character limit) and pick the avatar. For the bio, banner, background color and showcase use “Edit story and theme”. The avatar frame is chosen from the ones you already have.
First check that you're on the right profile: each profile has its own list and progress. Switch profiles and see if it's there. Also check that you're online.
If the progress is still missing, tell the team which title and which profile, and they'll check.
The showcase displays, on your profile, the favorite title or franchise you choose, for people who visit you.
To delete the account or ask about your data, talk to the team through Support: they take care of it.
In the Forum you can create topics and comment. The basics are asked: respect, no insults and care with spoilers. If you see something wrong, use the report option.

The forum has five layers, each with its own space: General (the community), Franchise (the whole universe, for example One Piece), Title, Season and Episode. This way an episode's conversation doesn't get mixed with general spoilers. You see and create topics in each layer through the Forum (with filters), through the Forum tab on the title's page, or through the player, on the episode you're watching.
Type @ and the person's name: suggestions appear and they get a notification.
You can upvote or downvote topics and comments, and “like” other people's reviews.
In the forum you can use bold (**like this**), italic (*like this*), strikethrough (~~like this~~), links and images, all with simple syntax.
If you see something offensive or spam, use the report option on the topic, comment or review, and pick the reason that best describes it. The team reviews it.
There's a translate button on topics, comments and reviews: it translates into your app's language with one click.
You can rate a title, a season or an episode, from 0.5 to 5 stars, and leave a comment. At the end of an episode a quick popup also appears for you to give a score.
You can follow other people on their profile. It's different from subscribing to a title, which is for getting alerts about new episodes.

k: how much xp do i need
l: You earn XP in two ways. 1) By action: watching an episode (2 XP if you mark it by hand; 100 XP when the app detects you really watched it, up to 20 episodes a day), subscribing to a title (30), rating (30), commenting (50), receiving an upvote (50), creating a topic (200) and getting a new follower (400, only once per person). 2) By achievements: each badge gives XP once (from 300 to 50,000, depending on rarity) and the monthly trophies give 10,000, 6,000 or 3,500. Levels get harder as you go up; the bar on your profile shows how much is left for the next one.

k: how do i see my achievements
l: Achievements unlock by themselves when you do certain things, like watching episodes, rating or commenting. There are four rarity levels and you choose which ones to show on your profile.

There are rankings by category: episodes watched, XP, reputation, topics, comments, achievements, coins, followers and list size. On your profile you see your position in each and whether you went up or down. At the end of each month the podium wins trophies.
The Shop sells coin packs, paid inside the app (card or PayPal). The price is always decided by the server, for security. Coins are for customizing your profile.
If the payment failed or the coins didn't arrive, open a support request in the Purchases category.
I'm sorry! Open a support request in the Purchases category and tell them what happened: the team will check the payment.
With coins you buy animated avatar frames and other profile customizations. You choose which one to use on your profile.

k: how do i add to my list
how do i see what i watched
l: In “My List” you organize what you're watching, what you want to watch and what you've finished, dragging titles between columns. To add one, press “My List” on the title's page.

k: when does an episode come out
how do i know when it comes out
l: If you press “Subscribe” on a title's page, I'll notify you when a new episode comes out. Alerts show up on the bell at the top.
In Settings you choose which alerts you want: replies, mentions, followers and new episodes. Check that you didn't turn them off by mistake.

k: when does the next episode come out
l: The calendar shows the releases of the titles on your list (including direct sequels of the ones you follow). On the page of a currently airing title you also see how long until the next episode.
The search at the top looks for titles and also people's profiles, and ignores accents. If you can't find a title, try the name in English or in romaji.
Titles from the same saga appear together on one card (a “franchise”), for example Naruto and Shippuden. Inside you pick the title or the season.
On the Anime page you filter by genre, format, airing status and year, and sort in several ways, all combined at the same time.
Some titles are for adults only: when you open the details a warning appears for you to confirm. It's there to keep everything clear.
On each series' page, next to the buttons, I show the official services where the title is available in your region. It only appears when there is data for your country.
AnimeLayer works on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and Android TV. You use the same account on all of them, and your list and progress follow you.
The app works on Android TV and you navigate it with the remote.
The app tells you when there's a new version and updates itself (on Windows and Android). If it doesn't update, close and open the app again.
If it still stays on the old version, tell the team which version you have and which system you're on.
On the computer, the app shows on your Discord what you're watching (title, episode and cover) for your friends. If you don't want that, turn off “Discord Rich Presence” in Settings, General tab.

In Settings, General tab, you can turn on “Minimize to tray” (instead of quitting, the app stays hidden next to the clock) and “Start with Windows” (it opens by itself when you turn on the computer). Both are optional and only exist on the computer.
At the top, next to your profile, there's the flag to change the app's language. It's available in 12 languages.
Sometimes the team puts the app under maintenance to improve things. It's usually quick: try again in a bit.
If it takes too long or the message isn't about maintenance, let the team know.
Close and open the app again and check that you have the latest version. If it always happens in the same place, tell me where and I'll pass it to the team.
That's a pain! Tell the team what happened: what you pressed, on which episode and whether a message appeared. The more details, the faster they fix it.
If you were punished, the message explains the reason. If you think it was a mistake, talk to the team through Support.

k: how do i contact the team
l: You can talk to the team through Support: you pick a category (Purchases, Customization, Badges, Forum or Other) and chat there, with the history saved.
I love ideas! Tell them to the team through support, in the Other category. Everything that arrives is read.
Using the app costs nothing. The Shop's coins are optional and are for customizing your profile.

At the end of each month (and each year) the rankings close: whoever is on the podium of each category wins a trophy, XP and a notification with the results. Trophies are kept in the Rankings tab of your profile.

k: why am i not earning xp
l: To prevent abuse there are daily limits on actions that give XP (for example, on automatically marked episodes and on comments). When you reach the limit, the rest of the day gives no more XP from that action; the next day everything goes back to normal.
In support you pick a category: Purchases (payments and coins), Customization (frames and profile), Badges, Forum, or Other for everything else. Choose the closest one; the team sees all of them.

The first message of the request is automatic (it comes as “AnimeLayer”); then someone from the team replies, and you see the whole conversation in the request itself. I can't tell you how long it takes, but you can continue the conversation while the request isn't resolved.
You sign in with the same account on any device and your list, progress and achievements follow you. Only the episode files stay on each device, temporarily.
The app needs internet for the catalog, your account and the episodes. There's no offline mode for now.
The basics: respect for other people, no insults, spam or harassment, and care with spoilers. The moderation team reviews reports and can mute or ban those who don't follow them.

k: how do i edit my comment
how do i delete my comment
l: You can edit your own topics and comments, and delete them as long as they don't have replies from other people yet (once someone replies, you can no longer delete). If you need help with a special case, talk to the team.

k: how do i use the app
l: Welcome! In a few steps: 1) you sign in with Discord or Google; 2) you pick or create a profile; 3) in Settings you add the addon you want to use to get sources; 4) you open a title and press to watch. The rest (list, alerts, forum, XP) you'll discover along the way.

It's a way of sharing files where people swap pieces with each other, instead of everything coming from a single server. The app handles it for you and plays the episode while it downloads. With this kind of sharing, your network address is visible to whoever is sharing the same file; if that worries you, you can use a VPN.

If you see “Invalid addon or unreachable URL”, check that the address is complete and correct (copy it again) and that the addon is online: when you open it in the browser, text with the addon's name should appear. If it says it's already installed, all good: you already have it. You just need to turn it on.
If it still fails, the addon may be down or have changed address. Try later, or use another address for the same addon.
Some addons have a configuration page. In Settings, on the Addons tab, the “Configure” button appears on those addons: it opens the addon's own page, where you make your choices.

addons_embutidos.t: Addons that come with the app
k: addons that come with the app
l: Three come with the app, always ready: LayerCatalog (search, lists and title pages), LayerSubs (extra subtitles in dozens of languages, with data from OpenSubtitles) and LayerTranslate (translates topics, comments and reviews with one click). Episode source addons are something else: those you choose and install yourself.
Settings has five tabs: General (tray, startup, downloads folder, cache), Addons, Notifications, Purchases (your history) and Updates (current version and news).
In Settings, on the Purchases tab, you see the history of your coin purchases. If you need a receipt or something is wrong, open a support request in the Purchases category.

In Settings, General tab, there's “Clear local cache”: it deletes the images and temporary data stored in the app. It's safe; the app downloads again what it needs. It usually fixes images that don't show.
In Settings, on the Updates tab, you see the version you have and the news for each version. They also tell you whether you have the latest.

When a new episode comes out for a title you follow, an alert appears on screen. If you don't like it, in Settings → Notifications turn off “Live New Episode Card”: you'll still see the alert on the bell.
In Settings → Notifications you choose each type: replies to your posts, mentions, new followers, topics and reviews from people you follow, and new episodes. You can turn each one on and off.

k: what is on the anime page
l: On a title's page you have tabs: Overview (synopsis and trailers), Seasons, Themes (openings and endings), Specials, Movies, Cast, Reviews and Forum. Movies, OVAs and specials are in the Specials and Movies tabs.
When they exist, trailers appear in the Overview of the title's page, with the video opening right there.
In the Themes tab of the title's page you see the openings and endings, with the song names, when the information exists.
In the Cast tab you see the title's main, supporting and background characters, with who voices them.

The catalog is updated automatically, so a very recent (or very obscure) title may not be there yet. Try the name in English or in romaji, and check it isn't inside a franchise. If it keeps missing, tell the team the name and they'll look.

Sometimes data sources bring wrong information or different numbering. The team can fix titles, images and descriptions by hand, per season or episode. Tell me which title and what's wrong in the support request.

Watching an episode downloads it and, since it's sharing between people, it also sends parts to others while you watch, so it uses a lot of internet. If you have a data limit on your phone, it's better to watch on Wi-Fi.
The player has a speed button (it shows 1.0x). You press it and pick faster or slower.

lista_episodios_leitor.t: Change episode without leaving the player
l: The player has the episode list: you open it, pick one and switch without leaving the video. The ones you've already watched appear marked.

forum_no_leitor.t: Forum and reviews in the player
l: The player has buttons to open the forum and reviews of the episode you're watching, without leaving the video.

Besides the subtitles that come with the source, LayerSubs looks for extra subtitles in dozens of languages (data from OpenSubtitles). Pick them with the player's subtitles button. If one is out of sync, adjust it or try another.

If there's no subtitle in your language, there's an automatic translation (beta): it takes an existing subtitle, in any language, and translates it keeping the same timing. You can see a preview to pick the best synced one.

k: what do you do with my data
l: By signing in you accept the Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy (they appear on the sign-in screen). We don't ask for a password: you sign in with Discord or Google. If you have questions about your data, talk to the team.

k: how do i create a topic
i want to create a topic
l: There are three ways. 1) In the Forum, press “New Topic”. 2) On the title's page, in the Forum tab: the topic is already linked to that title. 3) In the player, the forum button opens the discussion of the episode you're watching, and you can create the topic right there. When creating you pick (or it's already picked) the level: general, franchise, title, season or episode.
If you're viewing the Forum filtered by a title, season or episode, the new topic stays in that context and the context appears locked. To change it, clear the filters first.
Home shows a big highlight at the top and several shelves: Continue watching, Trending now, Popular this season, the next season and All-time popular.

barra_lateral_obra.t: What I see beside a title
k: how long until the next episode
l: On a title's page, on the side, you see the next episode (with the countdown), your progress, the technical details, what the community thinks, featured discussions and similar titles.
On the title's page you see the studio and its other works. This list grows as people open more titles from the same studio.
In the sidebar of a title's page the titles most recommended by the community to people who liked that one appear, with the affinity percentage next to them.
Reputation goes up when other people “like” your reviews. It's one of the ranking categories.
AnimeLayer only uses the dark theme, for now: it's nicer for watching episodes. If there's ever a light theme, we'll announce it in the news.
The app doesn't save episodes to watch later: it downloads while you watch and then cleans up the temporary files by itself. To watch, you need internet.
As far as I know, the app doesn't cast to the TV yet (Chromecast or AirPlay). You can use it directly on an Android TV, or connect your computer or phone to the TV with a cable.

Good question, and I'm no great critic, but I know where to look! 1) On Home, check Trending now and Popular this season. 2) In the Calendar, you see what's airing today among the titles on your list. 3) On the Anime page, filter by genre and sort by popularity. And “Continue watching” keeps your spot.

The forum is divided into layers (general, franchise, title, season and episode) precisely to help: the episode one only talks about that episode. Whoever posts should be careful; if you see spoilers without a warning, report it.
Profiles are public: other people can see your name, bio, banner, featured achievements and showcase. So avoid putting personal data in the bio.

The account is the Discord or Google one you sign in with, and there's no AnimeLayer password. To change the email, change it on that account. To sign in with another account, sign out and sign in again with the one you want.

Each person signs in with their own Discord or Google, and each account can have several profiles with their own list and progress. If you're sharing the app at home, profiles solve it: one per person.
Search the name in the bar at the top (it looks for titles and also profiles), or press the person's name in a topic or comment. On their profile you can see their achievements and follow them.
In the Forum you can sort topics by recent, popular or trending, filter by tag, show only those that don't have a reply yet and search by text. You can also filter by title, season or episode.

ordem_ver.t: In which order to watch a franchise
l: Inside a franchise, the Seasons list shows each title's order, and the movies and specials are in the Movies and Specials tabs. For a special order (chronological, without fillers), ask in the franchise forum: the community loves that topic!

In Settings, on the Addons tab, you see the ones you installed: tap to enable or disable and use the trash icon to remove. You can have several active at the same time: the app joins the sources from all of them and sorts them for you.

k: where to watch anime for free
l: I don't point to any, and that's on purpose: AnimeLayer doesn't bring or suggest addons, to stay out of the sources. The choice, and the responsibility, belong to whoever installs them.

I understand the curiosity, but the answer stays the same: I don't point to sites or addons. What I can do is show you, on each series' page, the official services where it's available (“Where to watch”).

Quality depends on the source: each one brings its own (480p, 720p, 1080p, 4K…). The source list has a quality filter. If only low versions appear, try another addon or wait: new episodes sometimes only have low versions at first. The image can look pixelated in fullscreen when the source is low quality.

It usually happens when two subtitles are active at the same time (for example, the source's one and an extra from LayerSubs). In the subtitles button pick just one. If it's the same subtitle repeated inside the source itself, try another track or another source.
In the player's subtitles button pick the option to turn them off. It stays saved for the next episodes.
When the sound doesn't match the picture, it's almost always that source: try another. If it happens on all of them, tell the team which system you're on and which title.

Black bars and a cropped image depend on the video's format and the screen (for example, a 16:9 video on a wider screen). Try fullscreen. If the image always appears stretched or cropped, tell us the title and the source.
In the player, the play/pause button is in the center of the controls. If the controls are hidden, move the mouse (or tap the screen) to show them.

k: how do i see my notifications
l: The bell at the top shows your notifications, with a counter of the ones you haven't seen. There's also a page with all of them.

We never ask for your password (you sign in with Discord or Google), payments go through Stripe and updates come from our own channels. If an antivirus warns about the app, tell us which one and which version, so we can check.
Yes! Besides anime, there's a CARTOONS section in the top bar, with cartoons and their franchises. They work like anime (list, forum, reviews), but stay out of the popularity rankings.
For now there's no version for iPhone or iPad. AnimeLayer works on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and Android TV.

quantos_perfis.t: How many profiles can I have
l: Each account can have up to 3 profiles, each with its own list, progress and XP.

k: how do i create an account
l: There's no separate sign-up: when you sign in for the first time with Discord or Google, the account is created. Then you create your first profile and you can start.

k: why does it ask for permissions
l: The app only asks for the essentials: internet connection (and seeing the network state) and, on Android, permission to install its own updates (that's why Android may ask you to allow AnimeLayer to “install apps”). It doesn't ask for camera, microphone, contacts, location or photos.
As far as I know, alerts appear inside the app (on the bell) and in the alert that pops up on screen while you use it. There are no system notifications for when the app is closed, for now.
The player controls hide by themselves after a while: move the mouse (or tap the screen) to see them again.
Every comment has the option to reply: your reply stays under the comment you answered, as a conversation. The person who wrote it gets an alert (if they have that notification on).
On your profile you see your activity and your forum statistics, like the topics you created. If you're looking for a specific conversation, use the Forum search.
Press your avatar at the top and choose “Log out” in the menu.

legal.t: Is it legal? Is it piracy?
k: where do the videos come from
is it a crime to use
l: AnimeLayer doesn't host or distribute videos and doesn't bring sources: it's an app to organize and keep track of what you watch, with a community. Sources come from third-party addons, chosen and installed by whoever uses the app, who is also responsible for what they watch. This isn't legal advice: find out about the rules in your country.
